description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:
We are looking for a Principal Enterprise Technology Architect to own the technical vision for how our internal business systems connect, scale, and evolve. This is a newly created senior Individual Contributor role: you will be the highest-ranking technical voice in our Enterprise Technology organization, setting the architectural standard that guides our team of experienced system administrators.

Crusoe is at an inflection point. We have mature, capable platforms running Finance (Oracle Fusion, Coupa, Sage Intacct), Construction and Operations (Procore, Oracle Primavera), and People (Rippling, Ashby), but they operate largely as islands. Your mandate is to design the unified architecture that connects them: defining master data models, engineering a scalable and increasingly event-driven integration layer, and building the governance frameworks (including how AI is responsibly introduced into these systems) that take us from startup agility to enterprise maturity.

This is a greenfield architecture role first. You will spend the majority of your time designing systems, producing ERDs, context diagrams, and sequence flows, before a single line of configuration is written. This role does not carry formal people-management responsibility, though as a Principal (P6) you may guide contributors indirectly on complex initiatives. You will serve as the integration and architecture subject matter expert that a team of senior administrators pulls in on complex, cross-system initiatives, and as a voice in Architecture Review Board discussions on major platform changes.

This role partners with, rather than replaces, existing domain owners: the IT Architect retains ownership of iPaaS design and governance, the Identity Lead retains ownership of IAM/PAM and access governance, and the AI & Automation Staff Engineer retains ownership of AI governance and architecture. This role's mandate is enterprise-wide data-model and integration-pattern design, done in partnership with those owners.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Greenfield Architecture & System Design

- Lead technical discovery for all major system initiatives, producing high-fidelity artifacts — ERDs, system context diagrams, data flow maps, and sequence diagrams — that serve as the source of truth for implementation

- Assess current platform limitations and define the path forward, including when to optimize, when to re-platform, and when to build a custom integration layer

- Serve as the primary technical evaluator during software procurement, vetting vendors on API robustness, data model flexibility, and security compliance — not just features

- Identify and document integration debt across the current-state architecture and develop a prioritized roadmap to address it

- Participate in Architecture Review Board discussions, ensuring major system changes align with enterprise standards and reference architecture

- Master Data & Integration Strategy

- Partner with platform SMEs and administrators to define a unified approach to master data across the organization

- Partner with the IT Architect and platform SMEs who own our iPaaS integration environment today, co-developing reusable integration patterns, error-handling frameworks, and self-healing workflows that raise the bar without displacing existing ownership

- Drive integration architecture toward API-first, event-driven patterns (REST, webhooks/pub-sub) where they improve reliability and reduce latency over batch processing

- Define how internal systems authenticate and communicate, with strict enforcement of secure API standards (OAuth 2.0, REST/SOAP) across all integrations

- AI & Intelligent Automation

- Partner with the AI & Automation Staff Engineer to identify high-value opportunities to embed AI into Crusoe's enterprise systems — workflow automation, intelligent document processing, enterprise copilots, and natural-language interfaces to platforms — contributing enterprise-systems and data-model expertise to their design

- Contribute enterprise-architecture perspective to the AI & Automation team's evaluation of agentic AI, RAG, LLM integration patterns, and orchestration frameworks (including MCP); co-develop governance standards for their use within enterprise systems alongside the AI & Automation Staff Engineer, who owns AI governance

- Partner with InfoSec and Data teams to ensure AI-enabled workflows meet data privacy, security, and audit requirements

- Cross-Functional Collaboration & Technical Advisorship

- Work alongside a team of experienced senior system administrators across Oracle, Procore, Coupa, Rippling, and other platforms — serving as the go-to architecture and integration resource on complex cross-system initiatives

- Conduct design and configuration reviews, provide architectural guidance, and help administrators think through integration trade-offs on their projects

- Establish shared standards for documentation, sandbox management, and change control that the broader team can build toward consistently

- Governance & Standards

- Establish the “Rules of the Road” for the Enterprise Technology team: naming conventions, sandbox management, documentation standards, and change control processes

- Partner with InfoSec to ensure all architectural designs meet SOC2 and SOX requirements

- Partner with the Identity Lead, who owns IAM/PAM and access design, to ensure RBAC models across enterprise systems are secure without creating operational friction — contributing enterprise-systems context rather than setting Identity policy independently

- Define architectural review processes and quality standards for enterprise-systems initiatives, coordinating with the AI & Automation and Identity teams on criteria within their respective domains

- Cross-Functional Translation

- Serve as the primary bridge between business needs and technical execution, representing the Enterprise Technology team to stakeholders in Finance, Construction, and People

- Communicate architectural trade-offs — real-time vs. batch, build vs. buy, monolith vs. modular — clearly to non-technical audiences

- Build credibility and trust with business partners through consistent, clear communication and follow-through

What You'll Bring to the Team:

About This Role:
The Mechanical Quality Inspector is a quality professional responsible for safeguarding product integrity across the entire manufacturing lifecycle—spanning Incoming Quality Control (IQC), In-Process Quality Control (IPQC), and Outgoing Quality Control (OQC).
Supporting both Modular Data Center (Spark) and Power Distribution Center (PDC) product lines, this role executes end-to-end inspections for mechanical and structural systems. From validating incoming raw components and structural assemblies, to performing in-process inspections and authorizing final ship release, the Quality Inspector ensures every product meets strict engineering specifications, safety codes, and customer requirements.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Incoming Quality Control (IQC): Inspect raw materials, structural steel, and sub-assemblies upon arrival against purchase orders, engineering specs, drawings, supplier CoCs (Certificate of Compliance), and supplier OQC reports to prevent non-conforming materials from entering production.

- In-Process Quality Control (IPQC): Perform designated hold-point inspections during structural fabrication and enclosure assembly. Ensure alignment and structural fit-up before downstream work continues.

- Outgoing Quality Control (OQC): Conduct comprehensive pre-shipment inspections on completed modular units including traceability & genealogy requirements. Verify final mechanical fit-and-finish, cosmetic quality requirements, printing & label accuracy, shipping bracing, weatherproofing, and loose-ship inventories prior to signing the final ship release.

- Non-Conformance & Root Cause: Identify, tag, and document non-conforming items (NCRs). Collaborate with Engineering, Production, and Quality Leadership to execute root-cause analyses and prevent defect recurrence (CAPA).

- Traceability & Documentation: Maintain complete inspection records—including hold-point sign-offs, torque logs, photo documentation, and shipping checklists—ensuring full unit traceability.

- Compliance & Continuous Improvement: Enforce compliance with ISO 9001 standards and applicable product and building code requirements (AISC 360, ASTM, AWS D1.1, IBC). Participate in Lean/5S initiatives to streamline inspection workflows and improve product quality trends.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

- Education Level: High School Diploma or GED required; Technical certificate or Associate’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, or Industrial Technology preferred.

- Professional Experience: 5+ years of experience in mechanical and/or electrical quality inspection in a heavy manufacturing, panel shop, or modular integration environment (an Associate's degree substitutes for 2 years of experience).

- Blueprint & Drawing Reading: Advanced capability to interpret mechanical assembly drawings, structural steel prints, piping/HVAC diagrams, and detailed bill of materials (BOMs).

- Technical & Precision Proficiency: Demonstrated experience using precision mechanical measuring tools (calipers, micrometers, protractors, laser levels, feeler gauges, calibrated torque wrenches).

- Dimensional Inspection: Expertise in dimensional inspections to verify part geometry, including bend angles and radius, flange lengths and hole locations.

- Structural Steel & Bolting: Knowledge of structural steel framing, high-strength bolting requirements (AISC/IBC standards for snug-tight, pretensioned, and slip-critical connections), and calibrated torque wrench application.

- Metal Composition Verification: Competence in analyzing material test reports (MTR) to validate metal alloy grades, sheet metal thickness, and material strength and chemical characteristics.

- Weld Inspection: Competence in visual weld inspection (welding symbols, defect detection like porosity, undercut, penetration) and reviewing Weld Procedure Specifications (WPS).

- Surface Coating Inspection: Expertise in performing paint/coating dry film thickness (DFT) measurements and verifying proper coating procedures are followed.

- Enclosure Integrity & Weatherproofing: Experience inspecting modular enclosure framing, structural lifting points/lugs, door alignment, weather seals/gaskets, and IP/NEMA sealing for outdoor environmental resistance.

- Digital & ERP Systems: Proficiency with MS Office/Google Workspace, digital Quality Management Systems (QMS), and ERP software.

- Physical Capabilities: Ability to maneuver around large modular units, work at heights, climb ladders, and inspect confined or hard-to-reach spaces.

- Safety & Compliance: Position is designated as safety-sensitive. Mandatory participation in company safety, drug, and alcohol programs.

Bonus Points:

- Mechanical / Structural Certifications: ICC Structural Steel and Bolting Special Inspector (S1), AWS Certified Weld Inspector (CWI) or formal non-destructive examination (NDE) training, NACE / AMPP Coating Inspector Certification (Level 1+), ASQ Certified Quality Inspector (CQI), or Lean Six Sigma Yellow or Green Belt.

- Direct exposure to industry standards including AISC 360, AWS D1.1, and IBC specifications.

- Familiarity with X-ray diffraction and other microscopic analysis techniques for copper parts management.

- Experience operating forklifts, overhead cranes, or rigging equipment.

- Electrical system knowledge including working knowledge of IEC, NEC, NFPA, IEEE, NEMA, or NETA ATS/MTS testing specifications, and the ability to identify electrical components, hardware, and equipment.

About This Role:
The Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE) is responsible for developing, managing, and continuously improving supplier quality performance to ensure purchased components, materials, and subcontracted processes consistently meet defined quality, reliability, delivery, and regulatory requirements.
Serving as the primary Quality interface between the company, suppliers, subcontractors, Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, and Operations, this role drives supplier qualification, New Product Introduction (NPI), process validation, corrective actions, supplier performance improvement, and continuous improvement across the supply base.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Supplier Quality Management: Own quality performance for assigned suppliers and commodities. Establish and maintain supplier quality requirements, specifications, and quality agreements. Monitor performance using defined KPIs, scorecards, and metrics while identifying risks and mitigation plans. Partner with Procurement and Engineering on supplier selection, development, and exit decisions.

- Supplier Qualification & Development: Participate in supplier qualification and selection. Conduct quality assessments, process audits, capability evaluations, and evaluate manufacturing processes, quality systems, and controls. Develop targeted improvement plans to bridge capability, capacity, and maturity gaps.

- New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, and suppliers during NPI. Review drawings, specifications, GD&T, CTQs, PFMEAs, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, MSA, SPC, and inspection plans. Drive DFM/DFA/DFR reviews, lead process validation, approve FAI/FAIR and PPAP submissions, and ensure production ramp readiness.

- Supplier Process & Product Quality: Perform process audits and manufacturing evaluations. Establish inspection and testing requirements based on product risk. Drive implementation of SPC, mistake-proofing, standardized work, and robust process controls, shifting suppliers from inspection-based quality toward prevention-focused quality.

- Nonconformance & Corrective Action: Lead supplier-related nonconformance investigations. Drive containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and preventive action (8D, CAPA, RCCA). Verify effectiveness of corrective actions to prevent recurrence and track issues through closure.

- Supplier Audits: Plan and execute risk-based supplier quality audits (process, product, system, special-process). Develop audit findings, oversee corrective-action plans, verify closure, and support internal, customer, and regulatory audits involving suppliers.

- Supplier Performance & Metrics: Develop and maintain quality metrics including incoming defect rates/PPM, NCR rates, FPY, CAPA closure, process capability ($C_p$/$C_{pk}$), COPQ, escape rates, and audit performance. Leverage data to identify systemic trends and continuous improvement opportunities.

- Incoming Quality & Manufacturing Support: Partner with Receiving and Incoming Inspection to establish risk-based inspection requirements, acceptance criteria, and disposition nonconforming materials. Work with Manufacturing Quality to resolve supplier-originating defects and reduce incoming inspection burdens through demonstrated supplier process capability.

- Supplier Change Management: Review and approve supplier process, material, equipment, tooling, location, and sub-tier supplier changes. Ensure appropriate qualification, validation, risk assessment, change control documentation, and traceability before implementation.

- Continuous Improvement: Lead supplier quality improvement projects using Lean Six Sigma and structured problem-solving methodologies. Reduce defects, scrap, rework, and supplier-related COPQ while promoting prevention-focused quality.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- Educational Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Quality Engineering, or related field.

- Professional Experience: 3+ years of experience in Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, or a related field, with direct experience working with manufacturing suppliers and subcontractors.

- Core Quality Tool Mastery: Strong knowledge of quality tools and problem-solving methodologies including PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC, MSA, 8D/RCCA, CAPA, and process audits.

- Engineering & Drawing Literacy: Proven ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, technical specifications, and inspection requirements.

- Analytical & Technical Problem Solving: Strong analytical capabilities to evaluate process capability, statistical data, and complex manufacturing defects.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, Operations, and external supply partners.

- Communication & Influence: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and external executives.

- Travel Flexibility: Willingness and ability to travel to supplier facilities as required.

- Safety & Compliance: Position is designated a safety-sensitive position located in safety-sensitive facilities. Mandatory participation in company safety, background check, drug, and alcohol programs is required.

Bonus Points:

- Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Supplier Quality Professional (CSQP), or similar designation.

- Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

- Frameworks & Methodologies: Experience with PPAP/APQP and structured automotive or aerospace quality methodologies.

- Specialized Manufacturing Processes: Experience with special processes such as welding, machining, fabrication, casting, forging, sheet metal, coating, or electrical assembly.

- Systems & Data: Experience with ERP/QMS software platforms and supplier quality dashboards.

- Operational Environment: Experience scaling supplier quality in high-growth manufacturing, NPI/ramp environments, or managing strategic subcontractors.

Reporting into Quality leadership, the QMS Manager partners closely with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and EHS to transition the organization from site-specific, paper-focused processes to a data-driven, risk-based, and preventive Quality Operating System. Operating across Manufacturing, QMS, Engineering, and Regulatory Compliance, the Manager will build and guide high-performing Quality teams to foster a rigorous Quality mindset across all Crusoe sites. This position requires approximately 30% to 40% travel among manufacturing facilities, vendor sites, and client locations.

- Multi-Site Manufacturing Quality Leadership: Direct quality operations across multiple Crusoe facilities. Define inspection standards and acceptance criteria, lead multi-site containment efforts with urgency, establish staffing requirements, partner with production leadership, coach quality staff, and build scalable quality systems to support rapid growth while owning QMS compliance and discipline.

- Product Change Management: Ensure all modifications to product designs and Bills of Materials (BOM) are formally communicated to Quality Assurance teams, systematically updating corresponding inspection protocols and acceptance criteria.

About the Role
You will spend your time making large language models run faster, cheaper, and more reliably in production. That means owning the inference stack end to end: profiling where time and cost go, bringing modern optimization techniques into real deployments, and getting deep into the serving code when the defaults are not good enough. This is core systems and performance work on some of the most demanding models in use today.

The work is applied, not academic. The optimizations you build land in real customer deployments, each with its own models, traffic patterns, latency targets, and cost constraints. So while performance is the heart of the role, you will also work directly with customer engineering teams to tailor deployments to their needs, take a workload from an early proof of concept to a fully monitored production service, and make sure the gains you engineer actually show up for the people running the workload.

To set expectations clearly, this is a hands-on engineering role built around coding, profiling, and low-level optimization. It also carries a customer-facing side, along with elements of product and technical solutions work, because that is where the performance work gets proven.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Bring current inference techniques into production and refine them.

- Design and optimize serving architectures, including prefill and decode disaggregation, request routing, and related approaches.

- Work down into the serving stack, from frameworks like vLLM and SGLang to the CUDA kernels underneath, profiling and running in-depth analysis to find and fix performance problems.

- Adapt and scale optimization methods across many kinds of ML models, with an emphasis on large language models.

- Profile and tune deployments against clear targets for latency, throughput, and cost, and keep them dependable under real traffic.

- Tailor deployments to each customer's models and constraints, partnering with their engineering teams to move a workload from an early proof of concept through to a live, well-monitored production service.

- Build and support the software and product features around the inference stack in a production setting, using one or more general-purpose languages, with Python preferred given how central it is to ML work.

- Experiment quickly: take fuzzy goals, shape them into clear specs and focused proofs of concept, run fast experiments to find what works, and ship well-tested results without delay.

- Own delivery end to end, from the first experiment through to the optimization running in production, keeping the underlying performance goals, clear specs, and follow-through front of mind, and drafting features and product requirement documents together with other engineering and product teams.

- Work through ambiguity and make sound calls on tradeoffs and tooling, steering away from complexity that is not needed.

- Take real pride and ownership in your work, hold yourself accountable, and look for the same from the people around you.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- A Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience shipping code in production with one or more general-purpose languages, such as Python or C++, with a strong preference for Python.

- Familiarity with methods for optimizing LLMs for high throughput / low latency inference.

- Comfort with modern LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang, and with profiling and analyzing performance down to the kernel level.

- A firm grasp of how GPUs are built and how they behave.

- Clear interest and hands-on experience with large language models.

- A working knowledge of AI/ML pipelines and the full path of developing and deploying ML models.

- Strong communication skills, particularly when explaining hard technical topics to customers and teammates.

Bonus points:

- A track record of making software systems run faster, especially for large language models.

- Experience with CUDA or comparable technologies.

- A strong command of software engineering fundamentals, with a record of building and shipping AI/ML inference systems.

- Experience with Docker and Kubernetes.

- Prior work building or tuning AI/ML projects, particularly in a customer-facing setting.

These are UL 891 listed, Engineered to Order assemblies built to hyperscale customer standards, with tight delivery windows and unforgiving long-lead component exposure.
This role is about throughput and material discipline. Switchboard programs live or die on breaker and bus availability, drawing approval turnaround, and clean work packet release to the assembly line. You'll own the full production path from customer submittal approval through factory acceptance testing and shipment, across a portfolio of concurrent orders.
You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with production supervisors, test technicians, and the materials team on the floor every day. Your work directly impacts our ability to energize compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources.
We are seeking an experienced professional with a proven background in electrical equipment or industrial manufacturing, a strategic mindset, and the persistence to drive submittal cycles and supplier commitments to closure. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

- Switchboard Manufacturing Execution: Own assigned switchboard orders end to end — submittal approval, engineering release, material readiness, assembly, wiring, test, and shipment.

- Submittal and Approval Cycle Ownership: Drive the customer submittal and drawing approval cycle to closure. This is the single most common source of schedule loss in electrical equipment and must be actively managed, not passively tracked.

- Long-Lead Material Management: Manage exposure on breakers, bus, metering, instrument transformers, and enclosures with Supply Chain against firm production start dates.

- Project Planning and Execution: Maintain the production schedule at work-order level in alignment with assembly line loading and plant capacity.

- Strategic Change & Risk Management: Process engineering changes and customer-driven revisions through impact analysis, pricing, and approval before floor implementation; ensure BOM and routing updates follow. Maintain risk logs, action logs, RFIs, submittals and change orders.

- Quality and Test Coordination: Partner with Quality leaders to ensure the Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) is executed on time and to the applicable standards and specifications, including production testing, non-conformance closure, and customer witness testing where required.

- Budget Reporting and Forecasting: Manage order cost performance — labor hours against estimate, material variance, and change order capture — and report against baseline. You own the accuracy of your order cost model, maintain it to the PMO reporting standard and cadence, and sign the monthly cost-to-complete position that feeds the program economics review.

- Logistics and Delivery: Coordinate shipment readiness: final inspection, documentation package, crating, and logistics alignment with customer receiving windows.

- Customer and Stakeholder Management: Serve as the day-to-day customer contact for assigned orders, including schedule reporting and change communication.

- Executive Dashboard Inputs: Complete the project-level portions of the sector executive dashboard on the published cadence — schedule position, milestone status, cost and margin position, and open risk. Your inputs are what gets reported upward, so their accuracy and timeliness are yours to own.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

- Industry Experience — Electrical Equipment Manufacturing: Experience with low-voltage power distribution equipment: switchboards, panelboards, bus systems, protective devices, and metering.

- Building Code & Electrical Code Knowledge: Competent in electrical code knowledge for collaboration with the in-house engineering department, manufacturing technicians, and customer engineers of record.

- Project Management Experience: Minimum of 3+ years managing projects within the electrical equipment, construction, engineering and/or manufacturing industry.

- Bachelor of Science: BS in Engineering, Industrial Technology, Construction Management or a closely related field.

This is a hybrid role by design. Modular is how Crusoe compresses the timeline from steel to compute, and that speed only holds if the controls package is repeatable, verified in the factory, and correct the first time it lands in the field. You will work alongside senior I&C engineers to develop the point lists, instrument schedules, and control system drawings that define the platform, then prove that work out on the factory floor through factory acceptance testing before a module ever leaves the building.
This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who wants to build depth in industrial controls inside a manufacturing environment rather than one-off site design. You will move between the design desk and the factory, translating standards into deliverables and then validating those deliverables against real hardware. Expect close mentorship from experienced engineers, clear ownership of your assigned deliverables, and increasing independence as your judgment develops. Denver is your home base, with estimated travel at 25% to manufacturing partners and deployment sites. This is a full-time position.

What You'll Be Working On

- Design Deliverable Development: Develop point lists, instrument schedules, I/O assignments, and control system drawings for modular data center systems under the direction of senior I&C engineers.

- Factory Acceptance Testing: Execute and document FAT protocols on control panels and integrated modules, including point-to-point verification, loop checks, and calibration confirmation prior to shipment.

- Manufacturing Support: Partner with manufacturing on the factory floor to resolve control panel build issues, wiring discrepancies, and instrument installation questions as modules move through production.

- Platform Standardization: Contribute to the repeatable design packages, drawing templates, and test procedures that let the modular platform scale across successive builds without rework.

- Vendor and Integrator Coordination: Support technical coordination with control panel fabricators, systems integrators, and instrument suppliers on submittals, specification compliance, and open technical items.

- Field Verification and Startup Support: Conduct field walks, equipment inspections, and basic calibration verification at manufacturing and deployment sites to confirm as-built accuracy and commissioning readiness.

- Documentation Integrity: Maintain accurate as-built drawings, test records, and instrument documentation so downstream construction, commissioning, and operations teams work from a reliable source of truth.

What You'll Bring to the Team

- Instrumentation & Controls Foundation: 2 to 4 years of professional experience in industrial instrumentation and controls, including exposure to point list development, control system drawings, and field instrumentation.

- PLC Proficiency: Working familiarity with Rockwell and Allen-Bradley platforms, including Studio 5000 and ControlLogix or CompactLogix hardware.

- SCADA Exposure: Hands-on experience with Ignition SCADA or a comparable platform, including tag configuration, screen navigation, and basic troubleshooting.

- Testing and Verification Discipline: Demonstrated ability to execute structured test procedures, document results accurately, and identify discrepancies before they propagate into downstream deliverables.

- Field and Factory Readiness: Comfort working in active manufacturing and construction environments, including field walks, panel inspections, and instrument verification alongside technicians and trades.

- Collaborative Judgment: A track record of applying established engineering standards independently while escalating technical ambiguity to more experienced engineers early and clearly.

- Mandatory Education: A Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Control Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Bonus Points

- Data Center or Mission-Critical Experience: Prior work on data center mechanical or electrical control systems, or in another high-availability industrial environment.

- Modular or Prefabricated Delivery: Experience supporting a productized or prefabricated equipment platform where design repeatability and factory verification drive schedule.

- Protocol Depth: Practical familiarity with Modbus TCP, BACnet, or OPC UA in a multi-vendor integration context.

- Industry Certifications: Relevant credentials such as network certifications, Rockwell or Inductive Automation certifications.

- OT Cybersecurity Awareness: Understanding of industrial network segmentation and OT security practices as applied to control system deployments.

- Mission Alignment: A genuine interest in energy and AI infrastructure, and in the engineering rigor required to build it at speed.

The Sr. Manager, Facility Operations – Colocation, North America is responsible for ensuring that every colocation provider supporting Crusoe Cloud across North America operates in full alignment with Crusoe Operations Standards. This role owns the operational governance relationship with colocation partners — from standards enforcement and compliance audits to incident management and vendor performance — safeguarding the reliability, safety, and security of the infrastructure that powers Crusoe Cloud. The ideal candidate combines deep mission-critical facilities expertise with strong vendor management skills and is comfortable operating as Crusoe's on-the-ground authority across a distributed, multi-provider colocation footprint.

Key Responsibilities
Operations Standards Governance & Compliance

- Own enforcement of Crusoe Operations Standards across all third-party colocation provider sites supporting Crusoe Cloud in North America.

- Conduct recurring audits, physical inspections, and documentation reviews of colocation facilities against Crusoe's safety, reliability, security, and environmental standards.

- Partner with the Global Data Center Operations Standards team to localize and interpret standards in light of NFPA (70/70E/72), NEC, OSHA, and applicable state/provincial and utility interconnection requirements.

- Own the tracking and timely closure of compliance gaps, audit findings, and corrective action plans (CAPs) in partnership with providers.

Colocation Partner Management

- Serve as the primary operational point of contact for coordination with each provider's facility operators, engineers, account managers, customer-service teams, and leadership across third-party colocation facilities across North America.

- Serve as Crusoe’s primary escalation point for maintenance, incidents, outages, service issues, chronic deficiencies, and provider performance.

- Own provider communications, escalation tracking, action items, and timely resolution of operational issues.

- Monitor service requests and ensure provider performance meets applicable Master Service Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

- Conduct regular site visits, facility walkthroughs, maintenance reviews, operational assessments, and meetings with provider leadership.

- Review provider staffing models, escalation procedures, preventive-maintenance programs, and emergency-response readiness.

- Lead governance cadences (monthly/quarterly business reviews) with providers, reviewing SLA performance, uptime, maintenance execution, and standards adherence.

- Provide operational input into Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, and SLAs, ensuring Crusoe Operations Standards are contractually reflected.

- Identify and escalate chronic performance, safety, or compliance issues, including formal partner risk assessments where warranted.

- Participate in and lead applicable Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs) and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with providers.

Facility & Technical Oversight

- Review provider electrical, mechanical, fire/life-safety, and physical security systems and operating procedures for alignment with Crusoe standards, with particular attention to high-density GPU compute environments.

- Oversee commissioning and acceptance testing of new colocation suites, cages, and data halls prior to Crusoe Cloud go-live.

- Review and approve Methods of Procedure (MOPs) and maintenance schedules for work impacting Crusoe-critical infrastructure.

- Support capacity planning, power/space utilization tracking, and growth forecasting in partnership with providers and internal Capacity Planning teams.

Incident & Risk Management

- Own Crusoe’s review of provider root-cause analyses and ensure all corrective and preventive actions are tracked through closure.

- Maintain a regional risk register for colocation facilities across North America and escalate material risks to senior leadership.

- Own Crusoe’s operational response and coordinate with colocation providers during incidents, outages, emergencies, and business-continuity events.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting

- Partner with Data Center Design & Construction, Security, Network/IT, Procurement, and Legal on colocation strategy, standards rollout, and contract renewals.

- Provide operational due diligence and standards input during evaluation of new colocation partners and markets in North America.

- Develop and maintain KPI scorecards for colocation provider performance and present regional performance and risk summaries to senior leadership.

- Champion continuous improvement, sharing lessons learned and best practices with the global Facility Operations and Operations Standards organization.

- Act as the operational link between third-party providers and Crusoe’s ROC, Cloud, Compute, Hardware, Reliability, Procurement, Legal, and leadership teams.

- Champion a safety-first culture across the third-party portfolio, including escalating work affecting Crusoe infrastructure when an unacceptable safety or operational risk exists.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Facilities/Mechanical/Electrical Engineering, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 8+ years of experience in mission-critical data center facility operations, including at least 3+ years managing multi-site or colocation-based operations at scale.

- Strong working knowledge of critical infrastructure systems: UPS, generators, switchgear, CRAC/CRAH and chilled-water cooling, fire/life-safety, and BMS/EPMS platforms.

- Proven experience managing third-party vendor and colocation relationships, including SLAs, MSAs, and governance cadences.

- Excellent stakeholder management, audit, and written/verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting risk and performance data to senior leadership.

About the Role:
Building on our team's single, secure, enterprise-grade data platform, this role owns the last mile - building out an AI-powered self-service analytics suite so the People team can make data-driven decisions in the flow of their work.

You will drive this adoption through a hybrid strategy. Enabling the People team on how to use our governed self-service suite with pre-packaged HR dashboards & insights built in Visier, as well as building their own content and analyses using Claude, connected to the same modeled data powering Visier.
As a Senior IC, you will own Visier outright, set the self-serve analytics roadmap, and have real latitude in how it’s built out. You will partner directly with Talent Acquisition, Employee Success Partners, Total Rewards, People Operations, and senior members of the People Science team to understand their goals and build the metrics, context, and AI-ready documentation that lets them find their own answers without waiting on an analyst.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Own the Visier Platform

- Serve as the technical and functional owner of Visier: configuration, metric definitions, security models, release management, and the primary POC for our vendor relationship.

- Build and extend Visier content (metrics, boards, alerts) and expand into new data subjects as we onboard new systems.

- Manage the integration between our data platform and Visier, partnering with Data Engineering on upstream models.

- Own data quality: define the checks, triage failures, and drive fixes back to the source system rather than patching them downstream.

- Drive AI & Self-Service Analytics

- Ensure consistency so an AI-assisted answer and a Visier dashboard always align. Evaluate AI outputs critically and know what missing context caused a wrong answer.

- Document data models, business logic, and known caveats. Treat context as a core deliverable to make the platform usable for both non-analysts and AI tools.

- Experience designing access and aggregation rules for sensitive people data, including comp and performance.

- Partner & Enable the People Team

- Act as an embedded partner to TA, Total Rewards, People Ops, and Business Partners. Conduct discovery, synthesize findings, and communicate insights up to the executive level.

- Move the function from ad hoc pulls to a durable reporting cadence built around meaningful organizational health and talent delivery insights

- Build and run enablement (training, office hours, documentation) to raise the data literacy of the HR function. Teach them how to explore data, interrogate AI generated insights, verify against sources of truth, and know when to escalate.

- Help build and deliver the self-service analytics roadmap. Translate business questions into deliverables, and know when to push back if the real answer is a process or systems or process fix rather than a dashboard.

- Bring a point of view. Connect the dots between business objectives and data

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- 4+ years in people analytics, HR technology, or a closely related role.

- Hands-on Visier experience: You must have gone through at least one implementation or meaningful capability expansion (deploying Visier or standing up new data subjects in an existing tenant).

- Strong SQL skills and comfort working directly in a cloud data warehouse.

- Fluency in the HR domain: you deeply understand recruiting, compensation, performance, and org structure, and know how underlying systems actually record this data.

- Demonstrated experience enabling others, whether through training, documentation, or converting a reporting backlog into self-service.

- A pragmatic approach to data governance. You know how to balance standardized dashboards for large audiences and enable exploration for your clients.

- Ability to work independently, prioritize concurrent workstreams, and handle sensitive data with total discretion.

Bonus Points

- Analytics Engineering capability: Experience with dbt, version control, CI/CD, and dimensional modeling. If you can own the transformation layer and not just the presentation layer

- Understanding of how to expose warehouse data to LLMs or agentic interfaces (semantic layers, MCP).

- Experience with our specific stack: Rippling, Workday, Ashby, Lattice, TeamOhana, BigQuery

- Experience using other BI platforms (Power BI, Tableau, Sigma) alongside Visier.

- Experience in high-growth or infrastructure environments where change is constant and part of the fun.

- Cell phone stipend

That means owning the inference stack end to end: profiling where time and cost go, bringing modern optimization techniques into real deployments, and getting deep into the serving code when the defaults are not good enough. This is core systems and performance work on some of the most demanding models in use today.

The work is applied, not academic. The optimizations you build land in real customer deployments, each with its own models, traffic patterns, latency targets, and cost constraints. So while performance is the heart of the role, you will also work directly with customer engineering teams to tailor deployments to their needs, take a workload from an early proof of concept to a fully monitored production service, and make sure the gains you engineer actually show up for the people running the workload.

To set expectations clearly, this is a hands-on engineering role built around coding, profiling, and low-level optimization. It also carries a customer-facing side, along with elements of product and technical solutions work, because that is where the performance work gets proven.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Bring current inference techniques into production and refine them.

- Design and optimize serving architectures, including prefill and decode disaggregation, request routing, and related approaches.

- Work down into the serving stack, from frameworks like vLLM and SGLang to the CUDA kernels underneath, profiling and running in-depth analysis to find and fix performance problems.

- Adapt and scale optimization methods across many kinds of ML models, with an emphasis on large language models.

- Profile and tune deployments against clear targets for latency, throughput, and cost, and keep them dependable under real traffic.

- Tailor deployments to each customer's models and constraints, partnering with their engineering teams to move a workload from an early proof of concept through to a live, well-monitored production service.

- Build and support the software and product features around the inference stack in a production setting, using one or more general-purpose languages, with Python preferred given how central it is to ML work.

- Experiment quickly: take fuzzy goals, shape them into clear specs and focused proofs of concept, run fast experiments to find what works, and ship well-tested results without delay.

- Own delivery end to end, from the first experiment through to the optimization running in production, keeping the underlying performance goals, clear specs, and follow-through front of mind, and drafting features and product requirement documents together with other engineering and product teams.

- Work through ambiguity and make sound calls on tradeoffs and tooling, steering away from complexity that is not needed.

- Take real pride and ownership in your work, hold yourself accountable, and look for the same from the people around you.

- Familiarity with methods for optimizing LLMs for high throughput / low latency inference.

About the Role:
As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will lead an engineering team focused on making large language models run faster, cheaper, and more reliably in production. While managing and growing the team, you will stay deeply technical and hands-on with the inference stack end to end: profiling performance, bringing modern optimization techniques into real deployments, and diving into serving code alongside your engineers. This role balances team leadership with core systems and performance engineering on demanding models in production.
The work is applied, not academic. The optimizations you build land in real customer deployments, each with its own models, traffic patterns, latency targets, and cost constraints. So while performance is the heart of the role, you will also work directly with customer engineering teams to tailor deployments to their needs, take a workload from an early proof of concept to a fully monitored production service, and make sure the gains you engineer actually show up for the people running the workload.
To set expectations clearly, this is an engineering leadership role that combines people management, technical direction, and hands-on coding and profiling. It also carries a customer-facing side, along with elements of product and technical solutions leadership, ensuring performance gains deliver clear business and customer value.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Bring current inference techniques into production and refine them.

- Design and optimize serving architectures, including prefill and decode disaggregation, request routing, and related approaches.

- Work down into the serving stack, from frameworks like vLLM and SGLang to the CUDA kernels underneath, profiling and running in-depth analysis to find and fix performance problems.

- Adapt and scale optimization methods across many kinds of ML models, with an emphasis on large language models.

- Profile and tune deployments against clear targets for latency, throughput, and cost, and keep them dependable under real traffic.

- Tailor deployments to each customer's models and constraints, partnering with their engineering teams to move a workload from an early proof of concept through to a live, well-monitored production service.

- Build and support the software and product features around the inference stack in a production setting, using one or more general-purpose languages, with Python preferred given how central it is to ML work.

- Experiment quickly: take fuzzy goals, shape them into clear specs and focused proofs of concept, run fast experiments to find what works, and ship well-tested results without delay.

- Lead team delivery end to end, guiding projects from early experiments to production optimizations, establishing performance goals, and partnering with product and engineering leaders on technical strategy and roadmaps.

- Work through ambiguity and make sound calls on tradeoffs and tooling, steering away from complexity that is not needed.

- Take real pride and ownership in your work, hold yourself accountable, and look for the same from the people around you.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- 2+ years of experience directly managing and leading an engineering team in a high-performance or ML-focused environment.

- Strong technical, hands-on experience in software engineering, low-level optimization, or ML infrastructure, with a continued desire to stay close to code and architecture.

- A Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience shipping code in production with one or more general-purpose languages, such as Python or C++, with a strong preference for Python.

- Familiarity with methods for optimizing LLMs for high throughput / low latency inference.

- Comfort with modern LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang, and with profiling and analyzing performance down to the kernel level.

- A firm grasp of how GPUs are built and how they behave.

- Clear interest and hands-on experience with large language models.

- A working knowledge of AI/ML pipelines and the full path of developing and deploying ML models.

- Strong communication skills, particularly when explaining hard technical topics to customers and teammates.

Bonus Points

- A track record of making software systems run faster, especially for large language models.

- Experience with CUDA or comparable technologies.

- A strong command of software engineering fundamentals, with a record of building and shipping AI/ML inference systems.

- Experience with Docker and Kubernetes.

- Prior work building or tuning AI/ML projects, particularly in a customer-facing setting.

We're looking for a Change Manager to deliver the people side of these transformations, ensuring that every employee, team, and leader is equipped, informed, and confident to embrace changes in the workplace. This role is critical to Crusoe's momentum: by minimizing resistance and driving adoption, you'll directly help our teams embrace change as a source of strength rather than disruption.

You'll partner closely with the workplace team and cross-functional partners to build readiness strategies, craft compelling communications, and coach employees through transitions — using proven frameworks like Prosci ADKAR to guide your approach. About the Role:
Crusoe is looking for a highly motivated and technically astute Senior Manager, Revenue Accounting to serve as the primary accounting lead for our most critical and complex revenue streams. This is a pivotal, build-from-the-ground-up role: you will directly impact our financial integrity and scalability by transforming raw deal information into robust, auditable accounting processes, and by advising Legal, Project & Cost Controls, Construction Managers, and Finance in real time as deal structures and business models evolve.
You will own the technical accounting positions on non-standard transactions, lead key aspects of the month-end close for your revenue streams, serve as a key contact for external auditors, and coach a team toward reaching sound technical conclusions independently. The ideal candidate is a licensed CPA who excels at deciphering intricate contracts, applying advanced US GAAP, and operationalizing solutions with minimal oversight — a self-starter who thrives in ambiguity. This is a full-time, exempt position.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Technical Accounting Mastery — Serve as the subject matter expert on all facets of technical accounting, including but not limited to ASC 606 and ASC 842. Proactively research, interpret, and apply other relevant GAAP guidance to unique transactions, documenting robust accounting positions.

- Contract Analysis — Bring an acute eye for detail to legal agreements, identifying subtle clauses, terms, and conditions that materially impact accounting conclusions (e.g., acceptance criteria, termination clauses, variable pricing, significant financing components, and principal vs. agent indicators).

- Coaching to Critically Think — Independently review, analyze, and provide feedback to your team so they learn to research and reach the right conclusions on highly complex technical matters themselves, rather than being handed the answer.

- Cross-Functional Partnership — Collaborate with Legal, Project & Cost Controls, Construction Managers, and Finance to provide real-time accounting guidance on deal structuring and evolving business models.

- Operationalization — Translate complex technical assessments into clear, actionable processes for billing, collections, and financial reporting teams, ensuring proper system setup and data flow. Build processes from scratch where none exist and lead automation and efficiency efforts where they do.

- Month-End Close Leadership — Lead and manage key aspects of the month-end close for assigned revenue streams, including journal entries, reconciliations, and flux analyses.

- Audit Management — Serve as a key point of contact for external auditors, preparing comprehensive documentation and clearly communicating complex accounting treatments.

- Continuous Improvement — Champion initiatives to enhance internal controls, improve data integrity, and drive automation across the revenue accounting function.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance required; Certified Public Accountant (CPA) certification required.

- Eight or more years of relevant accounting experience.

- Deep and demonstrable expertise in US GAAP, particularly ASC 606 and ASC 842, with a proven ability to apply guidance to highly complex, non-standard transactions.

- Exceptional contract review and analysis skills, with the ability to identify critical accounting implications from legal documentation.

- Proven track record of independently researching technical accounting topics, forming well-reasoned conclusions, and documenting robust accounting memoranda.

- Demonstrated experience operationalizing accounting processes, driving efficiency, and implementing controls in a fast-paced environment.

- A self-starter with an unwavering sense of ownership and the ability to navigate ambiguity with confidence and minimal supervision.

- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex accounting concepts clearly to diverse audiences, including senior leadership and non-finance teams.

- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

About the Role:
Crusoe builds cloud infrastructure for AI workloads. Cloud Monitoring Services owns observability across Crusoe Cloud: metrics, logs, alerting, and the telemetry agent that runs on every node in the fleet. Our customers run large, demanding AI training and inference workloads, and they depend on us for a clear, trustworthy view of what their infrastructure is doing.

We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Platform team: the time series and log storage systems, and the query layer that serves every dashboard, API call, and investigation on top of them. This is a first-line management role reporting to the Engineering Manager for Cloud Monitoring Services. You will take direct people management responsibility for a team of 4 to 6 engineers, growing, and own how telemetry is stored, retained, and read back at fleet scale.

This is a people-first leadership role with real delivery stakes. You will bring the technical depth to guide hard calls and earn your team's trust, but your success is measured through what your team accomplishes. Query latency, retention, and storage cost are live tradeoffs your team will be making continuously, and customers feel all three directly. The role sits alongside peer managers who own telemetry collection and the ingestion pipeline, and together you run a platform that has to work end to end. This is a full-time position.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Grow and develop your team. Manage 4 to 6 engineers directly: 1:1s, career growth, performance, and team health, with the team growing over time.

- Own storage and query. Be accountable for the time series and log storage systems and the query layer on top of them, including how they behave under load and how much they cost to run.

- Own delivery. Plan and sequence work across a roadmap that mixes customer-facing feature work with storage and query infrastructure, and make honest calls early when a plan is at risk.

- Set the technical direction for your area. Partner closely with the Staff engineers who own technical direction across the platform, so they can focus on engineering rather than absorbing delivery and handoff work alone. Ask the hard questions and make sound tradeoff calls alongside your engineers.

- Keep the operational bar high. Query is on the critical path when something is wrong in the fleet, so availability, query performance, and correctness of what comes back are core to the job, not afterthoughts.

- Own the team's oncall rotation and the operational health of the storage and query stack.

- Manage cost and scale together. Retention policy, downsampling, cardinality, and storage tiering are product decisions as much as engineering ones, and you will be in those conversations.

- Coordinate across team boundaries. Your team consumes what the collection and ingestion teams produce and serves internal platform teams as well as external customers, so sequencing dependencies and escalating early is a core part of the job.

- Shape the team over time. Work with recruiting on sourcing, run a high-quality interview loop, close strong candidates, and onboard them well.

- Collaborate across functions. Partner with product, neighboring infrastructure teams, peer managers, and leadership to keep priorities aligned as the observability product expands.

What You'll Bring to the Team:
We know great engineers and leaders come from many different paths. If you're excited about this work but don't match every point below, we'd still love to hear from you.

- You care about people. You want the engineers around you to grow, you give feedback that's both direct and kind, and you measure your own success through your team's.

- Technical depth. 5+ years of hands-on engineering experience, ideally in backend or distributed systems: databases, storage engines, query engines, streaming pipelines, or other data-intensive services (Go, Rust, Java, or C++ environments), and hands-on familiarity with Kubernetes. This role stays close to the technical work.

- Experience managing engineers. 2+ years managing software engineers directly, including owning performance cycles and career conversations. This team has an active roadmap and live customer commitments, so we are looking for someone who has run a team through delivery before.

- Experience coaching senior and staff-level engineers, and comfort partnering with strong technical leads rather than competing with them.

- A track record of shipping. You've delivered multi-phase projects against fixed deadlines, and you know how to keep infrastructure work moving alongside feature work rather than letting one crowd out the other.

- Operational judgment. You've run a team that owns a system customers depend on during an incident, and you know what it takes to keep that system trustworthy.

- Strong communication and judgment. You can align people across functions, explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical partners alike, and give your team clarity about what matters and why.

Bonus Points

- Experience with query engines and query cost control: planning, pushdown, caching, concurrency limits, and protecting a cluster from expensive queries

- Experience with retention, compaction, downsampling, and storage tiering for large telemetry or event datasets

- Familiarity with log storage and search systems: Loki, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, or similar

At Crusoe, the Capacity Planning & Efficiency team operates at the critical intersection of all Crusoe products, services, and underlying physical infrastructure. This role owns the integrated planning system itself - the connective tissue that turns long-range strategy into a committed, buildable, fundable plan. You will run the end-to-end planning rhythm across every resource class: GPU and accelerated AI fabrics, compute, storage (File, Object, and Block), network, and the data center power and space that gates all of it. You will own long-range planning, the integrated business planning cycle, allocation and constraints planning, the operating calendar, and the supply chain and financial commitments that flow out of them.

This is a single pane of glass role. Where domain planners go deep on one resource, you go wide across all of them and arbitrate - reconciling demand signals against supply commitments, hardware lead times, site readiness, and capital and operating budgets into one defensible plan the company runs on. You will not own any single resource domain; you own the system that reconciles them all, and the calls that fall out of it when supply is short. You will partner directly with Finance to translate the capacity plan into demand capex and opex forecasts, and you will be the person leadership turns to when a constraint, a slip, or a demand surprise forces a re-plan. This role is uniquely positioned to maximize fleet utilization with company-wide impact, directly supporting Crusoe's mission to align the future of computing with environmental sustainability.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Long-Range Capacity Planning: Own the multi-year outlook across GPU, compute, storage, network, and the power and site energization schedules that gate all of it, and build the scenario models - demand cases, technology transitions, refresh and decommission waves - that inform where Crusoe commits capital and builds next.

- Integrated Business Planning: Run the IBP/S&OP cycle end to end - demand review, supply review, reconciliation, and the executive decision forum. Maintain both the unconstrained demand signal and the constrained committed plan; the gap between them is how Crusoe sizes what it is leaving on the table.

- Constraints & Bottleneck Planning: Maintain a live model of what is actually binding - silicon allocation, supplier lead times, power energization, rack and network availability, deployment labor - quantify the impact of each, and drive every mitigation to a decision.

- Allocation & Arbitration: Own the framework that decides which demand gets which capacity when supply is short - prioritization rules, trade-off analysis, and a clean escalation path when the call has to go to leadership.

- Plan of Record & Operating Calendar: Design and run the planning calendar that synchronizes Cloud Engineering, Supply Chain, Data Center Operations, Product, and Finance. Govern the plan of record - commitment time fences, what is frozen versus still movable, and what triggers a re-plan.

- Demand & Bookings Translation: Convert contracted commitments, backlog, ramp schedules, and on-demand growth into resource-level forecasts, including the attach ratios that link GPU capacity to storage, network, and compute. Manage forecast accuracy and bias as owned metrics.

- Supply Chain Integration: Translate the plan into supplier commitments, purchase timing, and buffer strategy, navigating global lead times and allocation constraints with Supply Chain and Server Hardware Engineering.

- Financial Integration: Interface directly with Finance and Product to drive demand capex and opex forecasts off the capacity plan, own the linkage to unit economics, depreciation schedules, and utilization targets, and explain the variances when plan and actuals diverge.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- Proven Integrated Planning Expertise: 8+ years in infrastructure capacity planning, IBP/S&OP, supply and demand planning, systems engineering, or technical program management, including end-to-end ownership of a recurring planning cycle. Strong candidates come from either deep infrastructure or formal planning backgrounds - we expect to teach the other half.

- Breadth Across Resource Classes: Technical fluency across compute, storage (File, Object, and Block), network, and accelerated computing, plus the power, space, and cooling constraints that govern deployment. Deep expertise in one domain is not required; holding your own with the people who have it is.

- Supply Chain Fluency: Practical experience with lead times, supplier allocation, buffer strategy, and converting a plan into committed purchase orders and delivered hardware.

- Financial Acumen: Comfort operating in capex and opex terms - building demand-driven capital forecasts and defending the numbers in front of Finance and leadership.

- Modeling Craft: Expert-level Excel or Google Sheets. You build models other people can inherit, audit, and run without you - clear structure, documented assumptions, versioned, and still trustworthy several quarters after they were built.

- Hyper-Growth Experience: Planning inside high-growth public cloud environments or massively distributed systems, where the plan changes and the rhythm still has to hold.

- Exceptional Influence & Communication: Structured narrative delivery, crisp documentation, and executive-grade presentations that turn a complex plan into a decision leadership can make in the room. You will run a planning cycle spanning five organizations without managing any of them, and escalate cleanly when alignment is not reachable.

- Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Mathematics, Data Science, or an equivalent technical field.

This role focuses on low voltage switchboard manufacturing and the skid integration of those switchboards into packaged assemblies. The scope includes: multiple concurrent orders run independently, integrated skid packages alongside standalone switchboard lineups, and direct accountability for the cost and schedule commitment on each. Power distribution programs live or die on submittal turnaround, long-lead component availability, and clean work packet release to the assembly line. You own all three, and you work shoulder-to-shoulder with production supervisors, test technicians, and the materials team on the floor every day.
Your work directly impacts our ability to energize compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources.
We are seeking a seasoned professional with a proactive approach, exceptional organizational skills, a proven background in electrical equipment or industrial manufacturing, and a passion for driving project excellence. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

- Project Planning and Execution: Set realistic project goals, develop comprehensive strategies, and maintain the production schedule at work-order level in alignment with assembly line loading and plant capacity to ensure on-time delivery.

- Submittal and Approval Cycle Ownership: Drive the customer submittal and drawing approval cycle to closure. This is the single most common source of schedule loss in electrical equipment and must be actively managed, not passively tracked.

- Long-Lead Material Management: Manage exposure on breakers, bus, metering, instrument transformers, and enclosures — plus skid structural and interconnect material — with Supply Chain against firm production start dates.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with estimating, engineering, procurement, production, and accounting teams to align project activities and resolve issues.

- Customer Communication and Management: Develop and implement effective communication strategies and provide regular updates to internal teams and external clients. Champion project change control, including customer change orders and requests for information.

- Budget Reporting and Forecasting: Manage order cost performance — labor hours against estimate, material variance, and change order capture — and report against baseline. You own the accuracy of your order cost model, maintain it to the PMO reporting standard and cadence, and sign the monthly cost-to-complete position that feeds the program economics review.

- Quality and Test Coordination: Partner with Quality leaders to ensure the Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) is executed on time and to the applicable standards and specifications, including production testing, non-conformance closure, and customer witness testing where required.

- Team Leadership and Mentorship: Provide coaching and guidance to team members, ensuring clear understanding of tasks and efficient execution.

- Resource Management: Identify and allocate necessary internal and external resources to ensure project success.

- Executive Update Inputs: Complete the project-level portions of the sector executive dashboard on the published cadence — schedule position, milestone status, cost and margin position, and open risk. Your inputs are what gets reported upward, so their accuracy and timeliness are yours to own.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

- Industry Experience — Low Voltage Power Distribution Equipment: Working knowledge of low voltage switchboards, panelboards, bus systems, protective devices, and metering. Competent in electrical schematic and electrical code knowledge for collaboration with the in-house engineering department, manufacturing technicians, and authorities having jurisdiction for permit processing. Modularized electrical skid integration is preferred.

title: People Programs Specialist (Contract)
description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:
We're looking for a People Programs Specialist to support the build-out of Crusoe's core talent programs - job architecture, performance management, and the systems that run them. Most of this work is in progress rather than established, so the role is closer to construction than maintenance.

This person supports the Talent Management team who owns these programs. Program design, stakeholder strategy, and business-facing decisions sit with the program owners. This role turns those decisions into finished work: a complete job profile library, a configured and tested Workday tenant, a review cycle that launches on time. That means moving between detailed build work and operational execution depending on the week — pressure-testing leveling logic across a large set of job profiles, drafting manager toolkits and FAQs, tracking a cycle to completion.

The complexity here comes from the population. Crusoe is vertically integrated, spanning land acquisition and power development, real estate and data center construction, hardware manufacturing, and software engineering. The workforce ranges from skilled tradespeople on job sites to electrical engineers commissioning facilities to ML researchers. A job family structure or performance framework that fits one group often doesn't fit another, and the failure points usually surface during the build rather than the design. We need someone who catches those and raises them early.

The role broadly supports People Operations & Strategy. It's a 12-month engagement covering the job architecture rollout, the Workday performance implementation, and two full review cycles.

What You'll Be Working On:

- Job architecture (build + rollout)

- Complete the remaining job family and leveling build — drafting job profiles, mapping roles, resolving gaps with COEs and business stakeholders

- Maintain the source-of-truth architecture files and handle the technical administration that keeps them accurate

- Support rollout: manager communications, FAQ and toolkit development, mapping review sessions, escalation triage

- Workday performance implementation

- Partner on configuration and testing of Workday performance appraisal — requirements documentation, test scripting, UAT coordination, defect tracking

- Build the process documentation and admin runbooks that make the system supportable after go-live

- Performance review support

- Support the operational backbone of review cycles: launch setup, population and eligibility logic, cycle monitoring, reminder cadence, completion reporting

- Troubleshoot in-cycle issues and act as first-line support for managers and ESPs

- Flex work

- Move between operational execution and program work as priorities shift — talent review support, career pathway documentation, program effectiveness reporting, ad hoc analysis

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- 3-6 years in People/HR programs, talent management, or HR operations

- Experience with job architecture, competency frameworks, or job profile management

- Strong documentation discipline and attention to detail

- Clear written communication for manager- and executive-facing materials

- Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-moving environment

- Active use of AI tools to accelerate drafting, analysis, and documentation

Bonus Points

- Bachelor's degree in HR, Organizational Development, Business, or equivalent experience

- Experience with Workday (HCM, Talent, or Performance modules).

- Lattice (or similar: Culture Amp, 15Five) administration

- Experience supporting a performance management redesign or system migration

Compensation Range
Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $50.00 - $60.00 per hour. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.
